Chapter 13 of 19

Eternal Night

older built fabric / forgotten spaces170 BPM
The story

Not every part of the city gets looked at. There are old brick buildings with sealed doors, empty windows, signs for shops that closed long ago, rooms nobody has opened in years, paintings on walls that no one walks past anymore. The Eternal Night is what happens where attention has withdrawn.

It is not a place on the map so much as a condition. When people stop looking at something, the night settles into it and stays, even at noon. Things get lost there: old art, old rooms, whole habits a neighbourhood used to have. This is the danger Terminal City works against, not a villain but a slow forgetting, and the Eternal Night is where you can watch it happening.

The crows still inspect its edges. The Repair People mark where it leaks. What exactly the Eternal Night does for the city is a question the city has not finished answering. Light goes in. Night stays.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
